title: Moshoeshoe becomes king
description: In the upheaval of the Lifaqane, Moshoeshoe gathers scattered peoples under his rule and begins to build the Basotho nation.

title: French missionaries arrive
description: Eugène Casalis and Thomas Arbousset of the Paris Evangelical Missionary Society arrive at Moshoeshoe's invitation and found the mission at Morija.

title: Treaty with the British
description: Moshoeshoe signs a treaty with the Cape governor Napier in which the British recognise the Basotho as allies against the Boers.

title: Battle of Berea
description: Moshoeshoe mauls a British expedition under Cathcart and then lets it withdraw, a celebrated mixture of victory and tact.

title: Free State wars
description: Three wars with the Orange Free State over land cost the kingdom much of its arable west, despite the repulse of the assault on Thaba Bosiu.

title: Treaty of Thaba Bosiu
description: Moshoeshoe cedes most of his kingdom's farmland to the Boers to end the second Free State war.

title: British protection
description: At Moshoeshoe's plea the British proclaim Basutoland a royal dominion and order the Boers off the land, saving the kingdom from extinction.

title: Convention of Aliwal North
description: Britain and the Free State fix the protectorate's boundary, halving the kingdom and losing it the fertile western lowlands.

title: Moshoeshoe dies
description: The founder dies in his eighties and is buried on top of his mountain fortress.

title: Annexed to the Cape
description: Against Basotho wishes, Britain hands the protectorate to the Cape Colony to administer.

title: Gun War
description: The Basotho rise against Cape forces sent to disarm them and keep their guns; the fight ends the Cape's attempt to govern the territory.

title: Back under Crown rule
description: Unable to control the territory, the Cape hands Basutoland back to direct British rule.

title: First elected legislature
description: A new constitution gives Basutoland its first elected legislative council.

title: Pre-independence elections
description: Chief Leabua Jonathan's Basotho National Party edges out the Congress Party in the first elections by universal suffrage.

title: Independence
description: Basutoland becomes independent as the Kingdom of Lesotho, a constitutional monarchy under Moshoeshoe II with Jonathan as prime minister.

title: Jonathan seizes power
description: Losing the first post-independence election, Jonathan annuls it and rules under a state of emergency for sixteen years.

title: Military coup
description: Major-General Justin Lekhanya ousts Jonathan in a coup backed by South Africa, which had blockaded the border.

title: King dethroned
description: The military government deposes Moshoeshoe II after a power struggle and puts his son Letsie III on the throne.

title: BCP sweeps elections
description: Ntsu Mokhehle's Congress Party wins every seat in parliament in the first free elections since 1970.

title: Moshoeshoe II restored
description: Letsie III abdicates in favour of his father, who is restored to the throne after five years in exile.

title: Moshoeshoe II killed
description: Moshoeshoe II dies when his car plunges off a mountain road, and Letsie III becomes king again a month later.

title: SADC intervention
description: After months of anti-government protests over a disputed election, South African-led troops enter Lesotho in Operation Boleas and heavy fighting guts parts of Maseru.

title: Thabane returns
description: Tom Thabane's ABC alliance wins the third election in five years and he becomes prime minister for a second time.
